22 // Filesystem adapter design notes:
23 // - A manifest is the portable boundary; live HANDLEs never leave this module.
24 // - Paths are UTF-16 at the Win32 boundary and UTF-8 inside serialized JSON.
25 // - File identity is volume serial plus file ID, never a filename heuristic.
26 // - Reading reparse metadata always uses FILE_FLAG_OPEN_REPARSE_POINT.
27 // - Directory enumeration does not descend through a reparse point.
28 // - An object rejected by filters may still be needed as a parent directory.
29 // - Sparse allocation is orthogonal to logical length and stream contents.
30 // - Named streams are independent byte streams, including directory streams.
31 // - A hardlink shares all streams, so the manifest stores those streams once.
32 // - Windows access checks are preserved; errors are never converted to data.
33 // - Privilege adjustment only enables privileges already present in the token.
34 // - A successful capture means every selected stream was completely read.
35 // - Restore validates names and chunks before creating any destination files.
36 // - Overwrite is opt-in and performed by same-directory file replacement.
37 // - Every object receives its recorded ACL; parent ACL propagation is suppressed.
38 // - This is a per-stream consistent capture, not a VSS database transaction.
39 // - A multi-file restore is not advertised as an all-or-nothing transaction.
40 // A handle always closes before any temporary file is renamed. This also keeps
41 // error paths exception-safe when NTFS rejects a privilege-dependent operation.

427 // Filter evaluation has a stable, documented order for useful preview reasons.
428 // Explicit path/name exclusion is checked before any positive predicate.
429 // Different predicates combine with AND; patterns within one field use OR.
430 // Path rules refer to manifest-relative paths, including each source basename.
431 // A literal directory path matches its entire subtree; name globs do not.
432 // Extension matching is independent from object type matching.
433 // Owner filters accept SID or resolved DOMAIN\user display names.
434 // File size bounds are inclusive and use logical size, not allocation size.
435 // Date bounds are inclusive and parsed as ISO8601, including timezone offsets.
436 // Attribute predicates operate on Win32 flags, not localized labels.
437 // Content searching preserves an overlap so matches may cross 1 MiB reads.
438 // Content means UTF-8 bytes; the program does not guess a file's text encoding.
439 // Change-since compares metadata; timestamps are not proof of content equality.

534 // A hard maximum bounds memory used by the entry list and preview UI.
535 // Cancellation is polled between objects and long content reads elsewhere.

630 // Sparse streams may contain long logical holes with no physical allocation.
631 // Query ranges in bounded batches; ERROR_MORE_DATA is a continuation signal.
632 // Each iteration advances strictly beyond the previous range to avoid loops.
633 // Allocated tail ranges are clamped to EOF because allocation is block-aligned.
634 // Non-sparse streams have one full-length range and therefore no implicit gaps.
635 // Zero-length streams have no ranges but still appear explicitly in the manifest.
636 // Logical holes read as zeros but should not consume backup data blocks.
637 // Allocation queries can return partial batches with ERROR_MORE_DATA.
638 // Advance from the last returned range rather than assuming a fixed stride.
639 // Non-sparse streams use the downstream path with one complete extent.

1134 // Preflight reads every referenced block before creating a restore root.
1135 // Selection reduces output paths but never bypasses manifest safety checks.
1136 // Directories are created before data; their ACLs and timestamps are restored last.
1137 // Only the current file is transactional; earlier completed files may remain.

1139 // Hardlink aliases are created after their canonical data object is committed.

1142 // Restore has three phases: selection/preflight, data/link creation, metadata.
1143 // Selection includes ancestors and required hardlink canonical data targets.
1144 // No target directory is created during block integrity preflight.
1145 // Existing directory structure may be reused, but ordinary files require an
1146 // explicit overwrite choice. A directory/file type mismatch is never coerced.
1147 // Existing directory ADS are refused because replacing them would bypass
1148 // the per-file temporary replacement strategy used for ordinary files.
1149 // Symlinks and junctions are created only after all ordinary file writes.
1150 // Per-file sibling temporaries make MoveFileEx a same-volume replacement.
1151 // Cancellation removes only the current temporary, never a completed file.
1152 // Directory times are final because adding children changes parent times.
